question.leadin: This man's political supporters were derogatorily nicknamed the descamisados, or "shirtless ones."
question.text: Name this populist president of a South American country who regained power in 1973 after being overthrown in 1955. This man legalized women's suffrage while being influenced by his wife, Evita.
question.clue: This politician's left-wing supporters were killed at an airport in the Ezeiza (ayz-ay-EE-zah) massacre.

swap.text: The US also occupied this country after the Spanish-American War, though they did not annex it. The CIA tried to use an exploding cigar and a tuberculosis-infected scuba suit to kill Fidel Castro, a Communist who led this country during the Cold War.
swap.clue: Diego Velazquez de Cuellar served in this country as its first colonial governor and his rival Hernan Cortes launched an expeditionary force to Mexico from this colonial holding.

question.leadin: The Mariel boatlift was a sharp increase in immigration from this country to the United States, which has utilized the "wet feet, dry feet" policy since 1995.
question.text: Name this Caribbean nation, to which Elian Gonzalez was repatriated in 2000.
question.clue: After leading an attack on the Moncada Barracks, a future leader of this country gave the speech "History Will Absolve Me."

swap.text: Forces under Antonio Jose de Sucre won this decisive 1824 battle to ensure Peruvian independence. Following this battle, Jose de Canterac signed a capitulation for the Royalist forces.
swap.clue: After San Martin gave his troops to Bolivar, the newly combined forces helped liberate Peru by winning this 1824 battle named for a city in the modern Huamanga Province. This battle's result led to the surrender of the main royalist resistance.

question.text: Following the fall of Peron's third wife Isabel in a coup, Jorge Videla's (HOR-hay BEE-del-ah's) government launched this campaign of violently repressing dissent.
question.answerHtml: Dirty War [or Guerra sucia; or National Reorganization Process; or Proceso de Reorganización Nacional]
question.clue: This campaign was rolled back under Reynaldo Bignone and was ended when the Radical Civic Union came to power.

swap.text: Napoleon was willing to sell the Louisiana territory because of this conflict, which ended his ambitions of a North American empire and lost him his claims on Hispaniola.
swap.clue: Polish deserters were spared from a slaughter of colonists after this event that was led by an Emperor who was supplanted by King Henri Christophe.

question.text: This Argentine liberator fought in the Peninsular War and was given the title "Protector of Peru." He was the winning commander at Chacabuco and Maipu, and helped liberate Chile from Spanish rule.
question.clue: This leader defeated Manuel Osorio alongside Bernardo O'Higgins at Maipu after winning at Chacabuco.

swap.leadin: Along with Liberal leaders Juan Alvarez and Ignacio Comonfort, this politician supported the Plan of Ayutla ("eye-YOOT-lah").
swap.text: Name this president of Mexico from 1858 to 1872. The tenure of this first Mexican president of indigenous origin saw both the Reform War and the occupation of Mexico by the French under Emperor Maximilian I ("the first").
swap.clue: As minister of justice under Igancio Comonfort, he issued a namesake law which restricted the roles of the church and army in government.

question.leadin: This city was nicknamed the "Sodom of the New World" during the Golden Age of Piracy.
question.text: Name this Jamaican city that was a haven for pirates until order was restored by Lieutenant Governor Henry Morgan. It fell from prominence after being devastated by a 1692 earthquake.
question.clue: Some of this city fell into the sea during a 1692 earthquake.

swap.text: Toussaint was a leader of a slave rebellion against the French in this island nation on Hispaniola.
swap.clue: This country was ruled by Papa Doc and Baby Doc Duvalier for much of the 20th century.

question.leadin: Answer some stuff about the geography of Ecuador.
question.text: Isabela, San Cristobal, and Santa Cruz belong to this scientifically significant island group 650 miles off the western coast of Ecuador, also known as the Colon Archipelago.
question.clue: This group of islands, the largest of which is Isabela Island and whose largest town, Puerto Ayora, is on the island of Santa Cruz.

swap.text: The Piratini Republic was proclaimed by Antonio de Sousa Neto, triggering this uprising against Pedro II. Giuseppe Garibaldi led the navy for the Piratini Republic during this war.
swap.clue: This conflict that began in 1835. The short-lived Juliana ("zhoo-lee-AH-nah") Republic supported the rebels in this conflict, who declared their own republic with capital at Piratini.

question.text: The Duke of Caxias ["kah-SHEE-ahss"] ordered a massive road to cut through this region to flank Paraguayan defenses. Quechua and Guarani armies fought with tanks in a later war between Bolivia and Paraguay over part of this oil-rich region.
question.answerHtml: Chaco [or Gran Chaco; or Dry Chaco; or the Chaco Plain; or Paraguayan Chaco]
question.clue: The Paraguayan government encouraged Mennonites fleeing Soviet persecution to settle in this region, where they founded the city of Filadelfia. Eusebio Alaya and Daniel Salamanca led countries in a conflict over this oil-rich region.

swap.leadin: This island's Layou Petroglyph Park preserves an ancient face of Yocahu carved by indigenous people before the 8th century.
swap.text: Name this island whose national hero Satuye, aka Joseph Chatoyer, led a Garifuna revolt against the British in the 1790s, twenty years after the peace ending their first war. This island now forms a country with an island chain where many rebels were exiled on Baliceaux, near Bequia.
swap.clue: Joseph Chatoyer became a hero of this Windward island after fighting against the British with French assistance. In 1979, this island gained independence along with the Grenadines.

question.text: The Zimmerman Telegram sought a German alliance with this Mexican President, who drafted the Plan of Guadalupe, broke with Zapata and Pancho Villa after Aguascalientes, and was targeted by Obregon's Plan of Agua Prieta.
question.clue: As a result, ´Alvaro Obreg´on's supporters plotted the Plan of Agua Prieta to end this man's rule, and he was killed in May 1920.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about people associated with interwar pan-Africanist organizations, like the International African Service Bureau in London.
swap.text: The IASB's organizing secretary Chris Brathwaite emigrated from this then-colony with the British merchant navy. Sandra Mason served as the first president of this Caribbean country when it became a republic in 2021.
swap.clue: The Bayley plantation was home to a 1816 rebellion of slaves here known as the Bussa Rebellion, and it was the first American location that Oloudah Equiano described.

question.leadin: Answer the following about the dissemination of Rousseau in Spanish America.
question.text: Cecilio Baez's 1910 study of this dictator may have begun the common view that he sought to implement The Social Contract in practice. The doctorate of this first leader of independent Paraguay was actually in theology.
question.answerHtml: Doctor Francia [or José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia; prompt on El Supremo or Karai Guazu]

swap.text: During the regime of Francois Duvalier, this leader of the Tontons Macoutes became known for his embezzlement and selling blood and cadavers to Western enterprises, for which he was known as "The Vampire of the Caribbean."

question.leadin: Alleging fraud after his loss in the 1970 general election, this dictator's supporters mobilized an armed wing of his National Popular Alliance, or ANAPO.
question.text: Name this military dictator of Colombia who was backed by the M-19 movement. This man's 1957 removal by the bipartisan National Front is said to have marked the end of La Violencia.

swap.leadin: The foremost intellectual leaders of this movement were Plinio Salgado and Gustavo Barroso, who authored Judaism Freemasonry and Communism.
swap.text: Name this fascist movement whose supporters often engaged in street brawls with communists led by Luiz Prestes. This ideology taught people to undergo the "Revolution of the Self" to become one with the Homeland.
swap.clue: Under the Black poet Arlindo Veiga ("ar-LEEN-doo VAY-ga"), the Patrianovists allied with a party named for this ideology whose blue flag had a capital delta in a white circle.
